Let \(x\) be the total number of stones. Since Kevin counts by 11s, \(x\) is a multiple of 11. If he messes up \(n\) times, each mistake lowers the count by \(2\), so

\[
x - 2n = 2007 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x = 2007 + 2n.
\]

We need \(x\equiv 0\pmod{11}\):

\[
2007 + 2n \equiv 0 \pmod{11}.
\]

Since \(2007\equiv 5\pmod{11}\),

\[
5 + 2n \equiv 0 \pmod{11}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
2n \equiv 6 \pmod{11}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
n \equiv 3 \pmod{11}.
\]

Also, \(n\) cannot exceed the number of 11-groups:

\[
n \le \frac{x}{11} = \frac{2007+2n}{11}.
\]

Thus

\[
11n \le 2007+2n
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
9n \le 2007
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
n \le 223.
\]

So \(n=3,14,25,\dots,223\). These are

\[
n = 3 + 11t,\quad t=0,1,\dots,20,
\]

giving \(21\) values.

\[
\boxed{21}
\]
